agent: leftovers wave, reader A (the right-click menu)
question: interface/rightclickmenu.gui's rightClickMenu: who makes it and what shows it, in the front end and in game; its rows and their order; empty_right_click_entry; the three items CRightClickBuildUnitsItem, CRightClickCloseItem, CRightClickReloadItem - text, click, greying; tooltips; how it closes; whether a player of the shipped game can see it.

structs.name: CRightClickItemInterface
structs.comment: The right-click menu's row interface (RTTI, no bases, 3 slots, all _purecall): slot 0 IsAvailable, slot 1 RefreshButton, slot 2 OnClick. Every row class puts it at +0 and a CStandardlistboxItem at +4. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.
structs.evidence: RTTI export: CRightClickItemInterface, no bases, one 3-slot table at VA 0x15CFCEC whose slots are all 0xB961D5 (_purecall). Each of the three item constructors writes 0x15CFCEC at +0 first (0x697ECD, 0x6982BF, 0x6986BD) and its own class's table over it later, so +0 holds nothing but the table pointer. What would show it wrong: a constructor of the interface writing a field.

structs.name: CRightClickBuildUnitsItem
structs.comment: A right-click menu row offering to build one unit type in one province (`right_click_entry`; text = the type's name). **Never made in the shipped game**: both fillers hand its constructor the nodes of a list that nothing fills. A click only sets +0x88, which closes the menu - nothing is built. Bases: CRightClickItemInterface +0, CStandardlistboxItem +4 (tables at +4 VA 0x15CFD0C and +0x20 VA 0x15CFD44). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
structs.evidence: Size: both fillers allocate 0x90 bytes before calling 0x697EA0 (`push 0x90` at 0x6757A2, 0x675860, 0x6F2B52, 0x6F2C10). Tables: the constructor writes 0x15CFCFC, 0x15CFD0C and 0x15CFD44 at +0, +4, +0x20 (0x697F93-0x697FA0), matching the RTTI export's three tables. What would show it wrong: another allocation site of another size.

structs.name: CRightClickCloseItem
structs.comment: The right-click menu's `Close` row (localisation key CLOSE). Added last, and only when the menu already has two rows or more. A click sets +0x80, which closes the menu. Bases as CRightClickBuildUnitsItem (tables +4 VA 0x15CFDE0, +0x20 VA 0x15CFE14). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
structs.evidence: Size: `push 0x88` before the call to 0x698290 at 0x6758ED and 0x6F2C9D. The constructor writes the GetText('CLOSE') rendering into `button` (slot 51, +0xCC). What would show it wrong: another allocation site of another size.

structs.name: CRightClickReloadItem
structs.comment: The right-click menu's `Reload: <file>` row - a developer's hot reload of the .gui file the interface element under the pointer came from. A click sets +0x80 (closing the menu) and hands +0x84 to ReloadInterfaceFile. Greyed while +0x84 is empty. Bases as CRightClickBuildUnitsItem (tables +4 VA 0x15CFEB0, +0x20 VA 0x15CFEE4). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
structs.evidence: Size: `push 0xA0` before 0x698690 at 0x6755F2 and 0x6F29A2; the last field, the Hoi3CString at +0x84, ends at 0xA0. What would show it wrong: another allocation site of another size.

structs.name: CFrontEnd
structs.comment: The front end (main menu) screen; RTTI bases CEU3Idler at +0 and CReloadDispatcher at +0xB0. Declared here for the three right-click menu fields; the rest of its layout is described only in function comments (CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd, CFrontEnd::Enter). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.
structs.evidence: RTTI export: CFrontEnd, tables at VA 0x15D458C (offset 0, 110 slots) and 0x15D4748 (offset 0xB0). No struct of this name in project.json or bicelib_findings.json (checked by name). Size deliberately omitted: CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd's comment says 0x8B0, which this reading did not re-check.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_FillRightClickMenu
addresses.comment: **Fills and shows or hides the in-game right-click menu** (`rightClickMenu`, +0x1D90), and in the shipped game **always hides it**. Called once, from CInGameIdler_HandleInput's right release with nothing selected, no unit rows and the left button up (0x6528EE), which first sets +0x1D94 to the graphical map's entry for the province under the pointer (when there is one) and **+0x1D98 to 0**. Clears `options` (listbox slot 23). Then: (a) with an element at +0x1D98 - an `empty_right_click_entry` spacer row and a CRightClickReloadItem for the element's type's file (+0x24 of CGuiType); (b) else with a province entry at +0x1D94 - the spacer, then, **only where the player's country both owns (+0x330) and controls (+0x338) the province**, one CRightClickBuildUnitsItem per node of a local CList, and where the province's cores (+0x344) include the player (GetPlayer, slot 23) one more per node of a second list - **but both lists are only ever constructed empty** (0x432630 zeroes them, nothing writes them before the walks), so no build row is ever made. Then, with **two rows or more**, a CRightClickCloseItem is added last, `options` is sized to (first row width + 20, (rows + 1) x row height + 7) - + 14 instead where there are exactly three rows - and the window shown (slot 13 of +0x18, then its slot 11); **with fewer it is hidden** (slot 14 of +0x18). In game (a) is dead (+0x1D98 is only ever written 0) and (b) yields the spacer alone, so the menu never shows. Starts 0x6754B0, `ret 4` at 0x675C96. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.2.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x6754B0-0x675C96 and decompiled it from a copy of the project. The branch test `cmp [esi+0x1D98], ebx` at 0x67555B, the +0x1D94 test at 0x67565F; owner/controller tests at 0x675780/0x67578C against g_CCurrentGameState's player id (+0xC34); the cores walk at 0x675820. The list: `lea eax,[ebp-0x68]; call 0x432630` at 0x675668 (0x432630 is four stores of zero and `ret`), and no instruction between there and the first walk at 0x675798 writes [ebp-0x68] or passes its address on; the second list is built by 0x432630 at 0x675837 and moved into it by 0x679AE0 (free the target's nodes, push the source's). Count tests: `cmp [eax+8],1; jle` at 0x6758E3 and `cmp [eax+8],3` at 0x675AAF. +0x1D98's writers, by a displacement scan of .text: 0x648581 (constructor, esi = 0 from 0x6474C3), 0x64FC94 (ebx = 0), 0x6528E8 (edi = 0) - and no `lea` of it; the same scan found both reads here (positive control). What would show it wrong: a writer of +0x1D98 through another base register, or a filler of the build lists reached through a pointer this reading did not see.

addresses.name: CFrontEnd_FillRightClickMenu
addresses.comment: **The front end's copy of CInGameIdler_FillRightClickMenu**, instruction for instruction, on CFrontEnd's fields: the menu +0xB4, the province entry +0xB8, the element +0xBC. Called once, from the front end's per-frame update (slot 1, at 0x6EE3B6), for any mouse event of the frame **while Shift is held (keyboard +0x1C slot 10) and the right mouse button is down (input +0x64 slot 11)**, with +0xB8 = 0 and +0xBC = the interface element under the pointer (the gui's +0x98). So here branch (a) is live: an element under the pointer gives the spacer, `Reload: <file>` and `Close` (three rows, 270 x 142 for 250 x 32 rows) and the window is shown; nothing under it gives no rows and the window hidden. The caller then moves the window to the pointer, pulled back by its size + 10 where it would leave the screen (window slot 42). Starts 0x6F2860, `ret 4` at 0x6F3046. It is not part of CFrontEnd::LaunchGame (rva 0x2F07A0), which the same update calls just before. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.3.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x6F2860-0x6F3046: the same calls and constants as 0x6754B0 at the same relative places (0x698690 at 0x6F29CC, 0x697EA0 at 0x6F2B76/0x6F2C34, 0x698290 at 0x6F2CBB, `cmp [eax+8],1` at 0x6F2C93) with [esi+0xB4]/[esi+0xBC]/[esi+0xB8] where the in-game copy has +0x1D90/+0x1D98/+0x1D94. The caller at 0x6EE370-0x6EE3B6: `cmp [esi+8], edi` (event kind 0, mouse), [ebx+0x1C] slot 10 (+0x28, the keyboard's byte +0x50 at 0xB4E120 - Shift), [ebx+0x64] slot 11 (+0x2C, 0xB4EAE0 `mov al,[ecx+0x95]`, the second byte of the per-button array the DirectInput poll at 0xB4E900-0xB4EA69 sets for buttons 0..2), then `mov [ebx+0xB8], edi(0)` and `mov [ebx+0xBC], [0x1A857D8]+0x98`. No jump from the start of the update reaches past this loop (checked over 0x6EDD60-0x6EE35B). What would show it wrong: DirectInput button 1 being other than the right button on this build, or the front end's event list not carrying mouse presses.

addresses.name: CRightClickBuildUnitsItem::CRightClickBuildUnitsItem
addresses.signature: CRightClickBuildUnitsItem* __stdcall CRightClickBuildUnitsItem::CRightClickBuildUnitsItem(CRightClickBuildUnitsItem* this, void* screen, CSubUnitDefinition* type, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment: A build row: the CStandardlistboxItem at +4 with the window `right_click_entry` made through the screen's gui (screen slot 16 then slot 14's slot 11) into +0x24; screen +0x2C, type +0x30, province +0x34; its tables; a CButtonObserverGlue<CRightClickBuildUnitsItem> at +0x38 (owner the row, plain click vcall_0x8 = slot 2) registered on `button`; +0x88 = 0; `button`'s text (slot 51) = the type's slot 6 (its name). The file's 'Send Merchant' is overwritten. `ret 0x10`. Its four call sites are in the two fillers, inside walks of lists that are always empty, so it never runs in the shipped game. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x697EA0-0x69809E (`ret 0x10`, this at [ebp+8], screen [ebp+0xC], type [ebp+0x10], province [ebp+0x14]); stores at 0x697F65/0x697F6A/0x697F8A; 'right_click_entry' at 0x697EC5, 'button' at 0x697FB2/0x698040; `call [edx+0xCC]` with the type's `call [eax+0x18]` result at 0x697FEB-0x698004; glue constructor 0x698AD0 with 0x698C90 (vcall_0x8). Callers by findRefs: 0x6757C6, 0x675884, 0x6F2B76, 0x6F2C34 only. The type being a CSubUnitDefinition is inferred (likely): its slot 6 (0x5A38A0) builds a string from the key at +8 through an out pointer, and IsAvailable tests its +0x2D (is_land) against manpower - no build row was ever made to watch.

addresses.name: CRightClickBuildUnitsItem::IsAvailable
addresses.comment: Slot 0: may the row be pressed. True only where the province's controller (+0x338) is the player's country, the player's manpower (+0xBCC) is at least 1.000 **or** the type is not a land type (+0x2D), and the province has no combat of kind 1 (CMapProvince::HasCombatOfKind). Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x698170-0x698285: g_CCurrentGameState made if absent; country = [0x1A855A4]+0x16C [player id +0xC34]; `cmp edx,[ecx+0xCA8]` (province +0x338 against the country's tag id); `cmp [ecx+0xBCC],0x3E8; jge`; `cmp [ecx+0x2D],bl` on +0x30; `call 0x4A6010` with edi = 1; `sete al`. Sole holder of 0x698170 is CRightClickBuildUnitsItem slot 0 (vtable.py --holding). What would show it wrong: +0xBCC on CCountry not being manpower (the record's name for it).

addresses.name: CRightClickBuildUnitsItem::OnClick
addresses.comment: Slot 2, what `button` and a choice of the row both reach: **+0x88 = 1 and nothing else** - no command, no build. The next frame's update sees the flag and hides the menu. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: 0x727120 is `mov byte ptr [ecx+0x88], 1; ret`, in one table only (CRightClickBuildUnitsItem slot 2, vtable.py --holding). Reached from the glue's vcall_0x8 (0x698C90, `jmp [eax+8]`) and from the +4 table's slot 4 thunk 0x698D00 (`sub ecx,4; jmp 0x727120`). What would show it wrong: another reader of +0x88 than the slot 10 getter 0x697E80.

addresses.name: CRightClickBuildUnitsItem::WasClicked
addresses.comment: Slot 10 of the CStandardlistboxItem table at +4: the row's clicked flag (+0x84 from the sub-object = the item's +0x88). The menu's owners ask it of every row each frame and hide the menu if any answers yes. Close and Reload hold the shared `mov al,[ecx+0x7C]` 0x697E90 instead (also CTableLedgerItem slot 5, so left unnamed). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.5.
addresses.evidence: 0x697E80 is `mov al, byte ptr [ecx+0x84]; ret`, held by CRightClickBuildUnitsItem's +4 table at slot 10 only. The callers through slot 10 (+0x28) on each row of `options`: CInGameIdler::Update at 0x656860, the front end's update at 0x6EE9E8, each followed by the hide (+0x18 slot 14) when any answered. What would show it wrong: a list row table at +4 whose slot 10 means something else elsewhere.

addresses.name: RightClickItem_RefreshButton
addresses.comment: Slot 1 of both CRightClickBuildUnitsItem and CRightClickReloadItem (one body, two sibling tables, so recorded class-free): with a window (+0x24), `button` is enabled (slot 46, +0xB8) where the item's slot 0 answers yes and disabled (slot 47, +0xBC) where it answers no. Run every frame through the +4 table's slot 11 thunk 0x698C70. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.5.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x698A00-0x698ACF: `cmp [esi+0x24],0`, `call [eax]` (slot 0), 'button' looked up through the window's slot 13, then `call [edx+0xBC]` or `call [edx+0xB8]`. vtable.py --holding: CRightClickBuildUnitsItem slot 1 and CRightClickReloadItem slot 1, nothing else. That +0xB8 enables and +0xBC disables is read from CRightClickCloseItem's refresh, which calls +0xB8 unconditionally on a row that is always pressable - inferred.

addresses.name: CRightClickCloseItem::CRightClickCloseItem
addresses.comment: The Close row: the CStandardlistboxItem at +4 with `right_click_entry` made through the screen's gui into +0x24; screen +0x2C; a CButtonObserverGlue<CRightClickCloseItem> at +0x30 (plain click = slot 2) on `button`; +0x80 = 0; `button`'s text = GetText("CLOSE") rendered in the game settings' colours ("Close"). The screen comes in ECX, the row on the stack, `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x698290-0x69852A: `mov ebx,[ebp+8]` (the row), `mov edi,ecx` (the screen, which the fillers load with `mov ecx,esi` at 0x675908 and 0x6F2CB8), 'CLOSE' assigned and GetText'd, `call [eax+0xCC]` on `button`, `ret 4` at 0x69852A. Callers by findRefs: 0x67590B and 0x6F2CBB only.

addresses.name: CRightClickCloseItem::OnClick
addresses.comment: Slot 2: +0x80 = 1, so the next frame's update hides the menu. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: 0x6985F0 is `mov byte ptr [ecx+0x80], 1; ret`; one holder, CRightClickCloseItem slot 2 (vtable.py --holding); the +4 table's slot 4 thunk 0x698CF0 jumps here.

addresses.name: CRightClickCloseItem::RefreshButton
addresses.comment: Slot 1: with a window (+0x24), enables `button` (slot 46, +0xB8) - Close is never greyed (its slot 0 is the shared ReturnTrue). Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.5.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x698600-0x698686: `cmp [ecx+0x24],0`, 'button' through the window's slot 13, `call [eax+0xB8]`, `ret` at 0x698686. One holder, CRightClickCloseItem slot 1. Slot 0 of its primary table is 0xA92590, ReturnTrue.

addresses.name: CRightClickReloadItem::CRightClickReloadItem
addresses.signature: CRightClickReloadItem* __stdcall CRightClickReloadItem::CRightClickReloadItem(CRightClickReloadItem* this, void* screen, Hoi3CString* file)
addresses.comment: The Reload row: the CStandardlistboxItem at +4 with `right_click_entry` into +0x24; screen +0x2C; a CButtonObserverGlue<CRightClickReloadItem> at +0x30 on `button`; +0x80 = 0; the file name copied into the Hoi3CString at +0x84; `button`'s text = "Reload: " + file - a literal, not a localisation key. `ret 0xC`. The fillers pass the element's CGuiType +0x24 string. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x698690-0x6988A7 and decompiled it: assignString into +0x84 from [ebp+0x10], operator+ of the literal 'Reload: ' (no GetText) handed to `button`'s slot 51, `ret 0xC` at 0x6988A7. That CGuiType +0x24 is the type's file name is inferred: it is the string straight after the name at +8, and the reload resolves it as a file.

addresses.name: ReloadInterfaceFile
addresses.comment: **Re-reads an interface file and tells whoever built windows from it.** Makes the reload registry (0x1B1665C) on first use. A name holding `.gui` that the file system does not find as given gets `interface/` in front; if it then exists it is parsed into the gui (0x1A857D8, its CPersistent slot 3 with a fresh CParseContext, 'UNNAMED_SESSION') and 0xA7D740 run on the gui. A name holding `.lua` is only looked for, as given and under `script\`. Then the name is looked up in the registry and slot 0 of every CReloadableInterface registered for it (0xA7E210 registers them - the in-game screen does so for interface/menubar.gui right after making the right-click menu) is called; the answer is true unless one of them answers false. Callers: CRightClickReloadItem::OnClick and the `reload` console command. The string is taken by value. Bare `ret` at 0xA7E805. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.6.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled from a copy of the project and checked against the listing: the '.gui' (0x15CC894) and '.lua' (0x15B7B54) searches through 0x50E4C0, 'interface/' and 'script\' prefixes, the CParseContext/Tokenizer construction, the registry find 0xA7EFB0 and the walk calling each entry's slot 0 with the AND. Callers by findRefs: 0x43B550 (ConsoleCmd_Reload) and 0x6989E6 only. Inferred rather than confirmed because the file system's slot 9 is read as 'exists' from how its answer is used, and the return value's meaning (true where nothing is registered) was not exercised.

addresses.name: ConsoleCmd_Reload
addresses.comment: **The `reload` console command** ("Reloads the gui or lua file", argument 'file name'), registered in the static command table - name 0x170B154, description 0x170B168, this handler 0x170B16C - so it has no call site. No argument: 'Please specify the file name'. A name without `.lua`: ReloadInterfaceFile(name), answering '<name> reloaded!' or 'Failed to reload the file'. A `.lua` name is looked for as given, then under `script/` and `script/country/`, and run in the Lua states ('Failed to find the file' where none has it) - that half not read further. The same reload the right-click menu's Reload row does. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.6.
addresses.evidence: The .data table at 0x170B150: 1, 'reload', ..., 'Reloads the gui or lua file', 0x43B1D0, 1, 'file name' - the only pointer to 0x43B1D0 in any section. Disassembled 0x43B1D0-0x43B601: the argument count from the vector of 0x1C-byte strings (`imul 0x92492493`), the four reply strings, `call 0xA7E400` at 0x43B550, bare `ret`s at 0x43B252 and 0x43B601. Padding at 0x43B602 and the next handler (ConsoleCmd_ReloadInterface, reader B's) at 0x43B610.

struct_fields.name: right_click_menu
struct_fields.comment: The `rightClickMenu` window (interface/rightclickmenu.gui), made by the constructor through the gui's slot 10 and hidden at once. Filled by CInGameIdler_FillRightClickMenu, polled every frame by CInGameIdler::Update (any row's slot 10 set hides it), hidden on a left release over the map. Never shown in the shipped game. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Written once, at 0x649504 (`mov [ebx+0x1D90], eax` after `call [edx+0x28]` on [ebx+0x60] with 'rightClickMenu'), then `call [edx+0x38]` on +0x18 (hide). A displacement scan of .text finds 21 accesses, all reads but that one: in HandleInput (0x652910-0x652BA7), Update (0x6567F6, 0x656879) and the filler.

struct_fields.name: right_click_province
struct_fields.comment: The graphical map's entry for the province last right-clicked with nothing selected (its +0xC the CMapProvince): the map (screen slot 15) +0x1DF0 array at the province's id (+0xD0). Kept when the right click is off the map; cleared on a left release. What the filler would offer build rows for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.2.
struct_fields.evidence: Writers: 0x64857B (constructor, 0), 0x6528DF (`mov esi,[eax+0xD0]`, slot 15 (+0x3C), `mov esi,[eax+esi*4]` from +0x1DF0), 0x652BBA (0). Reader: 0x675657, which takes `[eax+0xC]` and compares its +0x330/+0x338 with the player and walks its +0x344 - CMapProvince's owner_id, controller_id and cores. The entry's own class was not identified.

struct_fields.name: right_click_element
struct_fields.comment: The interface element the right-click menu would offer to reload (CFrontEnd +0xBC's twin). **Only ever written 0** in game - the right release clears it just before filling - so the Reload row never appears in game. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.2.
struct_fields.evidence: A displacement scan of .text: writers 0x648581 (constructor, esi = 0), 0x64FC94 (ebx = 0, beside 'chat_window'), 0x6528E8 (edi = 0, before the call to the filler); readers 0x67555B and 0x67560D. No `lea` of it anywhere. The type is from CFrontEnd's twin, which holds the gui's +0x98 element, and from the filler reading its +0x24 (CGuiObject::type).

struct_fields.name: right_click_menu
struct_fields.comment: The front end's `rightClickMenu` window, made by CFrontEnd::Enter and hidden at once; filled by CFrontEnd_FillRightClickMenu on Shift with the right button held, polled and positioned by the front end's update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.3.
struct_fields.evidence: CFrontEnd::Enter 0x6EFFDE-0x6F0051: 'rightClickMenu', `call [eax+0x28]` on [edi+0x60], `mov [edi+0xB4], eax`, then `call [edx+0x38]` on +0x18. Read in the front end's update at 0x6EE42B-0x6EEA01 and throughout the filler.

struct_fields.name: right_click_province
struct_fields.comment: The front end's copy of CInGameIdler +0x1D94; set to 0 before every fill, so the front end's menu never offers build rows. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.3.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [ebx+0xB8], edi` with edi 0 at 0x6EE3AA, before the call at 0x6EE3B6; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd zeroes it at 0x6ED6AF (esi = 0 from 0x6ED68B). Read by the filler at 0x6F2A07.

struct_fields.name: right_click_element
struct_fields.comment: The interface element under the pointer when Shift and the right button opened the menu (the gui's +0x98); its type's file is what the Reload row offers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leftovermenus.md, section A.3.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x6EE39D-0x6EE3B0: `mov ecx,[0x1A857D8]; mov eax,[ecx+0x98]; mov [ebx+0xBC], eax`.
